name: Painting PC
summary: Painting PC is a PC-port of OISOI's Painting VR game. The game keeps a handful of the game's brushes and its realistic painting experience. Additionally the game includes a commission system where people ask you to paint something specific whereafter you gain currency and followers that progress you through the game.
contributions: For Painting PC, besides a quick hand here and there during polish, I was the only programmer working on the project. Thus besides the already existing brushes and painting system, I worked on every aspect of the game.

highlights.title: Commissions system
highlights.description: In the game players can accept commissions from clients in their phone. These are small conversations the player has with the client with potential diverging paths. Every message that has been sent, both from the player and commissioner, are saved to be viewed at any time.

highlights.title: Game savefile system
highlights.description: Since the player was able to progress in the game I had to create a savefile system. As the game was already released and some bigger features where still being worked on, I had to make sure that these older game files would still work with the newer versions.

experience: It was quite exciting working on Painting PC, as I was the sole programmer a lot of responsability was laid in my hands. I think what I learned most out of this project was to build modular. Especially during its first few weeks where the vision of what the game would become wasn't yet clear, I had to make features that were configurable enough to be build further upon later. This was also the biggest hurdle I had during development.

name: Painting VR
summary: Painting VR is the most rated painting simulation app on the Meta VR platform. It has an extensive set of brushes and tools and allows for highly realistic brush strokes. Players can also enjoy painting in a handful of diverse environments. The game gets frequently updated with new features, brushes and tools.
contributions: When I started my internship at OISOI this is the game I was initially put on, I helped clear out bugs and polish existing features. Over time I was allowed to develop new features on my own. When I officially started working at OISOI I was put on different projects, but every now and then I was put back on Painting VR to help the lead developer finish some bigger updates.

highlights.title: Brush packs
highlights.description: I developed the system behind buying in-game brush packs. These were DLC's that added a pack of new brushes to the game which you could access from your inventory.

highlights.title: Creativity booster
highlights.description: An empty canvas can be quite intimidating, stopping players from painting anything. To resolve that issue I developed the creativity boosters. These are random shapes and blobs that can be cycled through that will then be printed onto the canvas when created. The blobs were made using metaballs which I learned to use earlier in my internship.

highlights.title: Paint bucket metaballs
highlights.description: In my internship I asked to work on something graphics programming related. I was allowed to try and improve the existing paint bucket's pouring mechanic by using metaballs. I managed to get a rough prototype working, but we decided to scrap the feature since it still needed some development-time which we didn't have at the time.

highlights.title: Brush importer tool
highlights.description: One of my tasks during the internship was to make a tool that would make it easier to create new brushes. The tool was made using Unity UGUI and got used when creating brush packs with simpler brushes.

name: Wait What's That
summary: Wait What's That (WWT) is a multiplayer VR pictionary game where the drawer needs to draw a word with a random twist and tool. These can range from drawing on a tv with a rubber chicken, to spraying on a canvas where your sprayed lines constantly disappear.
contributions: At first I was placed on WWT for only a short while to help with the final polish steps before release. Then later when the player count started going up, I returned to fix a bunch of bugs. After I mainly worked as solo dev (I got some help towards the end of the bigger updates) to implement a new dedicated lobby environment, as well as implementing handtracking including some new tools.

highlights.title: Social lobby
highlights.description: To help players socialize and make friends, we decided to implement a social lobby hosted by a dedicated server. I worked on setting up the server on a virtual machine and made sure players correctly connected to it.

highlights.title: Handtracking
highlights.description: The studio signed a contract with Meta to implement handtracking into WWT, I was in lead for this assignment. The player's fingers and hands were tracked and made the character's hands move. This also needed to be synchronised, so some time was spent making sure the syncing didn't take too much bandwith.

highlights.title: Best Belgian multiplayer game
highlights.description: WWT got nominated to, and won, the Best Belgian Multiplayer Game Award in 2025 where we competed against 2 other games. It was quite the honor to be able to receive this award together with the team. I hope it's the first of many more awards to come!

name: Vandalizer
summary: Vandalizer is a high quality multiplayer VR grafitti game where you can spray paint on different objects. Each object is contained within a card which you can unlock by playing.
contributions: I helped develop this game during its earlier phases, back when we still had a different vision of the game. I mainly worked on smaller features and fixing bugs, sadly not a lot of these features made it through the final game.

name: Deep Engine
contributions: Since this is my own engine, I made everything!

name: Project Kame
summary: Project Kame is a platformer where you try to reach the end of the level before the timer runs out. The player has 2 different weapons they can use to get through the level. Every time the players die they gain power-ups to help progress the level, at the cost of a lower final score.
contributions: Project Kame was the last group project I made in DAE. We were commissioned by a duo to create a prototype version of one of their game ideas, which they hoped would kickstart their own indie studio. In this project we were with 2 programmers, I mainly worked on the enemies in the game, the swimming movement, the power-up system and the game loop system. I also made sure we delivered a proper working build every week.

highlights.title: Enemy behaviour
highlights.description: The game has a few different enemy types, I made sure each of them moved and attacked as designed. I remember struggling somewhat with the movement behaviour of the ants, but eventually I managed to create something pretty decent.

name: Dig Dug
summary: In Dig Dug you need to defeat all the monsters to be able to progress towards the next level. This is possible by either blowing them up using your pump, or curshing them underneath a falling rock. This project is a recreation of the original game made by Namco.
contributions: Dig Dug is my final exam's project of the Programming course in DAE, I made the game in a custom engine we created throughout the course. We used a few libraries, for example for the rendering-pipeline, the rest was programmed ourselves.

highlights.title: Level creation
highlights.description: Each level in the game was made using an external software program called " ". These would then be exported into a simple file which would be read when loading the game to load the levels

name: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
summary: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets is a simple demo recreation of the original game released by EA. In this game you solve simple puzzles and defeat enemies to progress through the level and reach the final star.
contributions: This project was my final exam for the Graphics Programming 2 course in DAE. We were given a game engine with a basic setup game loop, during the course we learned how to create the rendering pipeline for the engine using DirectX 11. I added functionality like: shadow maps, particle emitters, deferred light renderer, model animators, HLSL shaders, post processing, ...

name: Medieval Madness
summary: Medieval Madness is the first big group project I worked on. It's 4-player couch game where every person controls a ragdoll-like character. The game is similar to Super Smash Bros. where you hit players to rack up damage. The more damage they have, the further they launch when hit. The goal is to be the last man standing by pushing every other player into spikes on the border of the map.
contributions: For this project we were with 2 programmers. I mainly worked on the character controls, focusing to make them as intuitive as possible. I also worked on creating the dragon, it flies over the map leaving behind a trail of fire, damaging anyone that gets caught in its spread.

name: Raytracer - Rasterizer
summary: Two simple demos demonstrating the result of what we learned during the Graphics Programming 1 course in DAE. One demonstrates a few meshes being rendered using a raytracer, each mesh using a different material. The other demonstrates a mesh being drawn using a rasterizing in DirectX.
contributions: Both of these demos were made from scratch. We learned how to build these renders up, learning something new every week, and applying it to our growing application.

name: Influence map chasing algorithm
summary: This project demonstrates a chasing algorithm which could be used for in-game AI, based on a research paper.
contributions: This project was the exam for the Gameplay Programming course in DAE. There we learned about different algorithms used to control NPC AI in games. Here I created a chasing algorithm based on an influence map. This would decide where to NPC should look when chasing the player without giving away the exact position, allowing for more natural feeling chases.
